issues.legal_issue: A receiver placed in charge of property under court orders retained possession of a mill that was later leased to a co-owner under a court-supervised arrangement.
material_facts: The court orders placed the receivers in charge of the property, including the relevant co-owners’ shares in the mills.
A later court-approved arrangement provided for the mills to be run by the parties under leases granted by the receiver.
The receiver leased the flour mill to a co-owner, who accepted possession from the receiver and agreed to return it when the lease expired.
issues.conclusion: Read together, the orders placed the flour mill in the receiver’s possession, and the co-owner operated it under the court-supervised arrangement.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed the appointment, subsequent directions, and compromise order together to determine the receiver’s authority and possession. The court’s directions made the leasing arrangement a means of running the mills under its supervision; the lessee’s acceptance of possession from the receiver and promise to return it were consistent with that arrangement.

rule.if: civil_suit_with_court_receiver and receiver_order_covered_the_property and court_later_authorized_leasing_under_supervision and lessee_received_property_from_receiver

predicates.civil_suit_with_court_receiver: A civil suit was proceeding in which the court had appointed a receiver over property.
predicates.receiver_order_covered_the_property: The court’s order placed the property in question within the receiver’s charge.
predicates.court_later_authorized_leasing_under_sup: The court later directed or approved an arrangement for the property to be run through leases supervised by the court.
predicates.lessee_received_property_from_receiver: The lessee accepted possession of the property from the receiver.

issues.definition: When a civil suit has a receiver charged with the property and the court later arranges for it to be leased under supervision, a lessee who takes possession from the receiver occupies it under that arrangement.

issues.legal_issue: A receiver appointed without a fixed end date and directed to continue until discharged does not automatically cease to hold office merely because a final decree is silent about the receivership.
material_facts: The appointment order did not specify that the receivership would end when the suit was decided.
The preliminary decree directed the receivers to continue until discharged.
The final decree did not address or discharge the receivers.
The final decree left open the possibility of further relief if the sale proceeds did not satisfy the claim.
issues.conclusion: The receivers continued in office and were entitled to function until discharged.
issues.legal_principle: Neither section 51(d) nor Order XL of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, prescribes automatic termination of a receivership on a final decree. The court applied the principles stated in Halsbury’s Laws of England, Kerr on Receivers, High on the Law of Receivers, and Woodroffe’s The Law relating to Receivers in British India: an appointment expressly limited to judgment ends then, but an appointment with no defined tenure continues until discharge; a court may continue a receiver after a final decree when the circumstances require it. No earlier judicial decision was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: civil_suit_with_receiver and receiver_appointment_had_no_fixed_end and preliminary_decree_required_continuance_until_discharge and final_decree_left_receivership_unchanged and further_claims_remained_possible

predicates.civil_suit_with_receiver: A civil suit was proceeding in which a receiver had been appointed.
predicates.receiver_appointment_had_no_fixed_end: The appointment did not specify an end date or state that it would end upon judgment.
predicates.preliminary_decree_required_continuance_: The preliminary decree directed the receiver to continue until discharged.
predicates.final_decree_left_receivership_unchanged: The final decree neither discharged the receiver nor changed the earlier directions concerning the receivership.
predicates.further_claims_remained_possible: The decree left a claim or further relief unresolved after the decree was made.

issues.definition: When a civil suit has a receiver appointed without a fixed end, the decree requires continuance until discharge, and the final decree leaves the receivership unchanged while claims remain possible, the receiver continues until discharged.

issues.legal_issue: A court may direct summary recovery of property through a receiver from a party to the suit who received it under a court-managed arrangement and expressly undertook to return it when the lease expired.
material_facts: The occupant was a party to the suit.
The receiver managed the estate and delivered the mill to the occupant under an agreed scheme for operating the mills.
The lease expressly required the occupant to return the mill to the receiver when the lease expired.
The lease expired, after which the court directed the receiver to take possession of the mill.
issues.conclusion: The court could direct the occupant to return the mill to the receiver without requiring the receiver to bring a separate suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XL, rule 1(1)(b) and rule 1(1)(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the court may remove a person from possession and confer powers on a receiver to manage and protect property. Rule 1(2) limits removal of a person who is not a party to the suit if no party has a present right to remove that person. The occupant here was a party and had taken possession under a court-managed scheme while expressly agreeing to redeliver the property. The court distinguished Krista Chandra Ghose v. Krista Sakha Ghose, Nanakchand v. Pannalal, and Loonkaran v. I. N. John, which concerned different claims or circumstances; it also referred to Sivarajan v. Official Receiver, Quilon District, concerning enforcement of an express undertaking to surrender possession.

rule.if: court_managed_estate_through_receiver and occupant_was_party_to_suit and receiver_delivered_possession_under_integrated_management_scheme and lease_term_had_expired and occupant_expressly_promised_redelivery

predicates.court_managed_estate_through_receiver: The court administered property through a receiver.
predicates.occupant_was_party_to_suit: The person occupying the property was a party to the suit in which the receiver was appointed.
predicates.receiver_delivered_possession_under_inte: The receiver delivered the property to the occupant as part of an agreed arrangement for managing or operating the estate.
predicates.lease_term_had_expired: The agreed period of the occupant’s lease had ended.
predicates.occupant_expressly_promised_redelivery: The occupant expressly agreed to return the property to the receiver when the lease ended.

issues.definition: When the court manages an estate through a receiver and a party occupies property under that management scheme, the court may direct summary recovery through the receiver after the lease expires if the occupant expressly promised to return it.
